name: query
title: Query Pluggy Documentation
description: Ask a natural-language question about the Pluggy API and get a generated answer with citations. Combines docs, changelog, recipes, and API reference. Responds in the user's question language.

question.description: The user question, in any language

locale.description: Preferred content language. Default: no filter (multilingual).

types.description: Content types to consider. Default: all.

includePrerelease.description: Include RC/beta versions. Auto-detected from question if omitted.

name: search_docs
title: Search Pluggy Documentation Guides
description: Search the Pluggy documentation guides (concepts, quickstart, integration). Returns reranked excerpts with relevance scores.

query.description: The search query, in any language

locale.description: Preferred content language. Default: no filter (multilingual).

limit.description: Max number of results to return (1-20).

name: search_changelog
title: Search Pluggy Changelog
description: Search the Pluggy changelog (release notes, breaking changes, migration notes). Returns reranked excerpts with the entry's publication date, language and the section heading the text came from, so results can be ordered by recency and cited precisely. Entries are published in English and Portuguese.

query.description: The search query, in any language

locale.description: Restrict to one language. Omit to search both — note that a month published in both languages then matches twice.

since.description: Only entries published on or after this date (YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD). This narrows a ranked search; for an exhaustive answer to 'everything that changed since X', use list_changelog_changes instead.

limit.description: Max number of results to return (1-20).

name: list_changelog_changes
title: List Pluggy Changelog Changes
description: Enumerate individual changelog changes — not whole months — filtered by type, breaking status, category or date. Exhaustive and deterministic, so an empty result genuinely means nothing matched. Use this for 'what broke', 'what shipped since X' or 'what changed in payments'; use search_changelog when the question is about wording rather than a filter. Structured months cover February 2026 onwards; older entries are free prose and are not listed.

since.description: Only changes published on or after this date (YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD).

until.description: Only changes published on or before this date.

breaking.description: true returns only breaking changes and deprecations.

endpoint.description: Only changes that touch this endpoint, e.g. 'GET /transactions' or just '/transactions'. Matched case-insensitively against the endpoints the entry declares — a month that declares none cannot match, and is counted in unstructuredMonthsSkipped.

product.description: Only changes tagged with this product area, e.g. 'open finance'.

category.description: Case-insensitive substring of the section heading, e.g. 'pagamentos', 'conectores', 'dashboard'.

locale.description: Language of the entries to read. Months are published in both, but not always at the same time; the response reports any month that exists in the other language and not this one.

limit.description: Max number of changes to return (1-200).

name: search_recipes
title: Search Pluggy Recipes
description: Search the Pluggy recipes (cookbook, integration patterns, code examples). Returns reranked excerpts with relevance scores. Recipes are English-only.

query.description: The search query, in any language

limit.description: Max number of results to return (1-20).

name: search_qa
title: Search Pluggy Curated Q&A
description: Search the curated, human-verified Pluggy support Q&A (real questions answered by the team, mostly in Portuguese). This is the highest-trust source for 'how do I / why does X happen' support questions — prefer it over the docs guides when a question matches. Returns reranked question+answer excerpts with relevance scores.

query.description: The search query, in any language

limit.description: Max number of results to return (1-20).

name: get_guide
title: Get Pluggy Documentation Guide
description: Retrieve the full content of a single Pluggy documentation guide by its slug and locale.

name: list_guides
title: List Pluggy Documentation Guides
description: List all available Pluggy documentation guides (slug, title, description, category) for a given locale. Optionally filter by category.

locale.description: The locale to list guides for. Default: 'en'.

name: get_api_endpoint
title: Get Pluggy API Endpoint Details
description: Retrieve full details about a specific Pluggy API endpoint by its operationId. Returns method, path, parameters, request body, and responses sourced from the OpenAPI spec. Defaults to the main Pluggy API; pass `spec` for another (e.g. 'enrichment-api').

spec.description: Which OpenAPI spec, by id or title. Default 'pluggy-api'. Options: pluggy-api, status-api, enrichment-api.

name: list_endpoints
title: List Pluggy API Endpoints
description: List all available Pluggy API endpoints from an OpenAPI spec. Defaults to the main Pluggy API; pass `spec` to target another (see list_specs — e.g. 'enrichment-api'). Optionally filter by tag (case-insensitive).

spec.description: Which OpenAPI spec to list, by id or title. Default 'pluggy-api'. Options: pluggy-api, status-api, enrichment-api. Call list_specs for details.

name: list_specs
title: List Pluggy OpenAPI Specs
description: List the available Pluggy OpenAPI specs. Use a spec's id with list_endpoints / get_api_endpoint to browse that API. There are two: the main Pluggy API and the Enrichment API (categorize / behavior-analysis / recurring-payments).

name: search_endpoints
title: Search Pluggy API Endpoints
description: Deep-search Pluggy API endpoints by keyword across path, operationId, summary, description, tags, and parameter names — to discover the right endpoint when you don't know its operationId. Searches every spec by default; pass `spec` to scope to one (see list_specs).

query.description: Keywords to match (e.g. 'create item', 'webhook', 'consent', 'categorize'). Case-insensitive; all words must match.

spec.description: Optional: restrict to one spec by id or title. Omit to search all specs.

name: execute_request
title: Execute a Pluggy API Request (GET)
description: Read from the Pluggy API with a live GET call and return the response. Provide either a full `url` or a `path` (+ optional `spec` to resolve the base URL). Safe and side-effect free: this tool cannot POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE — use create_request, update_request or delete_request for those. Target API: the **Pluggy API** (https://api.pluggy.ai) plus its siblings enrichment-api.pluggy.ai and status.pluggy.ai — no other host can be reached. Reference: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/reference. Paths are freeform, so discover the right one with list_specs / search_endpoints / get_api_endpoint before calling instead of guessing. Authentication is NOT injected — pass your own credentials in `headers` (e.g. { "X-API-KEY": "…" } for enrichment-api, or { "Authorization": "Bearer <apiKey>" } for the main API).

method.description: Optional, and only GET is accepted — this tool performs nothing else. Use create_request (POST), update_request (PUT/PATCH) or delete_request (DELETE) for writes.

url.description: Full request URL (must be an https Pluggy API host).

path.description: Path to call (e.g. '/items'), combined with the spec's server URL when `url` is omitted.

spec.description: Spec id/title used to resolve the base URL for `path` (default 'pluggy-api').

headers.description: Request headers, including your own auth (e.g. X-API-KEY or Authorization). No credentials are added for you.

name: create_request
title: Create via a Pluggy API Request (POST)
description: Make a live POST call to the Pluggy API — creating a resource or triggering an action (items, connect tokens, webhooks, enrichment runs). This WRITES to real data, so confirm the endpoint and the body with get_api_endpoint first. Reads go through execute_request; updates through update_request; deletions through delete_request. Target API: the **Pluggy API** (https://api.pluggy.ai) plus its siblings enrichment-api.pluggy.ai and status.pluggy.ai — no other host can be reached. Reference: https://docs.pluggy.ai/en/reference. Paths are freeform, so discover the right one with list_specs / search_endpoints / get_api_endpoint before calling instead of guessing. Authentication is NOT injected — pass your own credentials in `headers` (e.g. { "X-API-KEY": "…" } for enrichment-api, or { "Authorization": "Bearer <apiKey>" } for the main API).

url.description: Full request URL (must be an https Pluggy API host).

path.description: Path to call (e.g. '/items'), combined with the spec's server URL when `url` is omitted.

spec.description: Spec id/title used to resolve the base URL for `path` (default 'pluggy-api').

headers.description: Request headers, including your own auth (e.g. X-API-KEY or Authorization). No credentials are added for you.

body.description: JSON request body (object/array); sent as application/json.

name: list_teams
title: List your Pluggy teams
description: List the teams your Pluggy dashboard account belongs to. Start here: pick a team, then use its id as `teamId` in the other tools. You can switch teams anytime by using a different team's id.

name: list_applications
title: List a team's applications
description: List the applications/environments under a team (from list_teams). Pick one and use its id as `applicationId` in data tools.

name: select_application
title: Select an application for this session
description: Validate an application and confirm the team + application to use. Call this after list_applications; then pass the same `teamId` and `applicationId` to the data tools for the rest of the conversation (call it again to switch).

annotations.title: Select an application for this session

name: get_application
title: Get an application's configuration
description: Read how one application is configured: its name, environment (sandbox or production), whether it is enabled, its clientId, allowed origins and Connect branding (title, logo, primary color). For webhooks use list_webhooks. Use this to answer questions like 'how is my app configured?' or 'is this app in production?'. Unlike list_applications (which lists a team's apps) and select_application (which only confirms the app to use for the session), this returns the full configuration of one app. The client secret is never included — it is only shown once, when it is generated in the dashboard.

name: list_connectors
title: List a team's connectors
description: List the connectors available to a team's application.

name: get_stats
title: Get a team's dashboard stats (for monitoring)
description: The core monitoring tool: the same stats the Pluggy dashboard shows, over any date range and filters, so you can answer 'how are my connections doing', compare periods, and spot anomalies proactively. Kinds: `items` (item counts by execution status), `items-by-connector` (the same split per connector/institution — use it for 'which banks are erroring most'), `syncs` (sync volume/outcomes), `syncs-lag` (how stale connections are), `connectors` (connector availability), `payments` (payment volume and outcomes), `payments-by-connector` (the same per institution). Filters: date range (startDate/endDate, ISO), a connector, error statuses, sandbox, connectors' `fromDay`, and payments' `paymentType`. To compare periods, call twice with different date ranges.

applicationId.description: Optional application id to scope the stats (from list_applications).

endDate.description: Range end (ISO date). Same kinds as startDate.

executionStatuses.description: Filter by item execution status, e.g. ERROR, CONNECTION_ERROR, CREATE_ERROR, MERGE_ERROR, LOGIN_ERROR (items / items-by-connector).

fromDay.description: For kind=connectors: window in hours (1 or 24).

paymentType.description: For kind=payments / payments-by-connector: only this payment type.

annotations.title: Get a team's dashboard stats (for monitoring)

name: get_item
title: Get one item
description: Get a single connected item (status + executions) by its id, scoped to a team.

teamId.description: The team id the item belongs to (from list_teams).

name: debug_item
title: Diagnose a failing item
description: Diagnose why a connected item is failing. Fetches the item's current status and its recent executions (sync attempts, error codes, timestamps) plus any open incident on its institution, so you can explain the root cause and the next step for the end user — e.g. expired credentials → reconnect / update the connection; consent expired or a resource not granted → re-authorize; MFA/user-input needed; or a provider-side/known-incident issue. Read the `status`, the latest execution's error, and the connector, then give a short plain-language diagnosis + suggested fix. When the item looks healthy but a PRODUCT came back empty, this tool cannot tell you whether the institution ever shared it: that lives in `GET /items/{id}/resources` on api.pluggy.ai (Open Finance items only), which you can read with execute_request using the caller's own API key — a resource reported `PENDING_AUTHORISATION` is the end user's to authorise at their bank, `UNAVAILABLE` is the institution's call, and `AVAILABLE` with no data on our side is the only case that is ours. See https://v2.docs.pluggy.ai/en/docs/connections/resources. To see what each recent sync actually brought — products with data or empty, entities returned, transactions created by date — use get_execution_reports. Do NOT expose internal ids or logs to the end customer.

teamId.description: The team the item belongs to (from list_teams).

name: get_execution_reports
title: See what an item's syncs brought
description: Per-execution breakdown of what a connected item's recent syncs actually brought. Use it when an item looks healthy (debug_item shows no error) but the user says data is missing. For each execution, newest first: its status, and a `report` with the products that came back with data, empty, or failed (`products`), how many entities the institution returned per product (`returned`: accounts by type, credit cards, bills, investments, loans, identity, and transactions per account type), and how many transactions were created, updated and deleted, with the created ones split by transaction date relative to the sync — today, yesterday, two or more days ago, future (`transactions.*.createdByDate`, Brazil time). `report: null` means the execution did not get as far as saving data, or its report is still being processed (it lands shortly after the sync ends). `products: null` or a `null` counter in `returned` means not measured (older executions), never zero. Pass `executionId` (from get_item / debug_item) for one execution; otherwise the `limit` most recent (default 10, max 50). Not the same as get_reports, which is the team's aggregate ingestion over a date range.

teamId.description: The team the item belongs to (from list_teams).

executionId.description: One execution of the item (from get_item / debug_item). Omit for the most recent ones.

limit.description: How many recent executions to include (default 10, max 50). Ignored with executionId.

annotations.title: See what an item's syncs brought

name: check_incidents
title: Check Status Page incidents
description: List Pluggy's current (and recently-resolved) Status Page incidents and maintenances — the same source as status.pluggy.ai. Use it to tell a customer whether a problem is a known provider-side outage. Optionally filter by a connector id (the Pluggy institution/connector) to see only incidents affecting that bank, or by infra component (api | webhooks | connect). Pairs with debug_item: if an item is failing and its institution has an open incident, the fix is 'wait for the incident to resolve', not a reconnect.

connectorId.description: Filter to incidents affecting this Pluggy connector/institution id.

component.description: Filter to infra incidents on this component.

includeResolved.description: Include recently-resolved incidents too (default: only active).

name: get_billing_url
title: Get the team's billing dashboard
description: Get a link to the team's usage and billing dashboard, with consumption and cost.

name: get_reports
title: Get transaction-ingestion reports
description: Get the team's transaction-ingestion report — a daily time series or a summary — over a date range, to understand data volume and ingestion health over time (and compare periods).

name: list_webhooks

name: list_webhook_events
title: List delivered webhook events
description: List recent webhook delivery events for a team/application — useful to debug 'did my webhook fire / did it fail'. Optionally scope by application.

applicationId.description: Optional application id to scope the events.

name: get_webhook_event
title: Get one webhook event

name: create_support_ticket
title: Open a Pluggy support ticket
description: Open a support ticket for a connector/data problem on one of your teams. Only enabled for teams with the partner ticket integration turned on. Use it for a REPRODUCIBLE problem on a specific item — one ticket per problem, not per affected end user. Always pass externalId (your own issue id) so retries don't create duplicates. Pass dryRun: true first to validate the payload without filing anything.

description.description: What is wrong, since when, how many users are affected, how to reproduce.

itemId.description: A Pluggy item id (UUID) where the problem reproduces. Must belong to the team; its connector determines the institution, so you don't pass one.

product.description: Affected product. One of: Identity, Accounts, Transactions, Credit Card, Investments, Authentication, Investment Transactions, Consent, Loans, Outro.

problemType.description: Closest problem type. One of: Transação da conta corrente não sendo retornada, Balanço da conta corrente sendo retornada incorretamente, Data da transação da conta corrente sendo retornada incorretamente, Campo recebedor e pagador não está sendo retornados (paymentdata), Transação da conta corrente sendo retornada duplicada, Transação do cartão de credito não sendo retornada, Compras parceladas sendo retornadas incorretamente, Conexão não esta sendo atualizada automaticamente, Transação do cartão de crédito sendo retornada duplicada, Transação do investimento não sendo retornada, CNPJ do investimento não sendo retornada, Balanço do investimento sendo retornado incorretamente, Investimentos sendo retornados com um status incorreto, Investimento sendo retornado sem o campo value, Investimento sendo retornado sem o campo quantity, Investimentos sendo retornados com dados incorretos, Identity não sendo retornada, Erro no consentimento, Conexão retornada com o status de PARTIAL_SUCCESS, Conta corrente não sendo retornada, Cartão de credito não sendo retornado, Investimento não retornado, Outro.

accountType.description: Pessoa Física | Pessoa Jurídica | Corretora | Outra

externalId.description: Your own issue id — idempotency key.

priority.description: P0 — Crítico | P1 — Alto | P2 — Médio | P3 — Baixo

dryRun.description: Validate only; do not create the ticket.
